rooms.5251: Heat beats from a broad stone basin in the middle of this low chamber, where a tongue of flame burns without wood or oil to feed it. The sandstone walls are scorched black and scored with old glyphs that seem to crawl in the shifting light. Fine sand trickles from the shaft overhead, where worn footholds climb up to the glare of the open desert. Beside the basin a square opening breathes cool, stale air, and narrow steps lead down into the dark.
rooms.5252: This cramped cell was cut from the bedrock and meant to stay hidden, its only way out a set of narrow steps climbing up toward the warmth and light of the fire chamber. Rows of tally marks cover one wall, scratched in groups of five until they run out of room. A stone bench is carved from the rock along the other side, polished by long use. The air is cool and dry, and every sound seems to die against the stone.
rooms.212005: Two squat towers of sun-bleached stone flank the West Gate, their arrow slits facing out over the dunes. Sand blows through the open gateway and drifts in ridges against the inner wall, where nobody has troubled to sweep it. West of the arch the paving ends and the Great Eastern Desert begins, shimmering in the heat. East of the gate, River Avenue leads into Port Halyon, smelling of mud, tar and the sea.
rooms.212056: River Avenue begins its run along the riverbank here, a broad street of cracked flagstones with a low wall on the water side. A painted sign of crossed swords hangs over a stout door to the south, where the Weapons Shop does its trade. The West Gate stands at the street's end to the west, sand drifting in beneath its arch. Eastward the avenue follows the river toward the heart of the port.
rooms.212057: Here the avenue runs close beside the river, and the smell of wet mud and weed rises over the embankment wall. Iron mooring rings are set into the wall at intervals, crusted with rust except where ropes have rubbed them bright. Across the brown water stand the backs of warehouses, their loading doors shut. The street carries on east toward Main Street and west toward the desert gate.
rooms.12026: The avenue widens before it meets Main Street, and the houses on its southern side grow taller and better kept. A gravelled lane leads south between iron railings into the Wealthy Neighborhood, where clipped hedges hide the gardens from the street. On the river side a stone horse trough stands half full of green water. The cobbles run on east to the crossing with Main Street and back west along the river.
rooms.12033: River Avenue ends here against Main Street, and a weathered milestone at the corner gives the distance to Garathorm in worn figures. To the north the street climbs onto the Main Street Bridge, its stone parapets white with salt and droppings. South Main Street runs on south between shuttered shops, and River Avenue leads away west along the water. The paving is grooved by cartwheels and dark with spilled fish brine.
rooms.212033: The Main Street Bridge carries the road across the river on three broad arches of weathered grey stone. Below, the brown water swirls around the piers and leaves a ragged line of weed and froth on each cutwater. The parapets are carved with leaping fish, worn almost smooth by wind and idle hands. The road runs north to the busier crossing by Wharf Avenue and south to the junction with River Avenue.
rooms.12032: Wharf Avenue branches off east here toward the quays, and the smell of fish, tar and wet rope rides along it on the wind. North Main Street climbs away north between tall merchant houses with carved balconies. To the south the road rises onto the stone hump of the Main Street Bridge. Beyond the rooftops the long arches of the old aqueduct stride across the skyline.
rooms.12030: The smell of fresh bread spills from the open door of the Bakery to the west, warm and heavy enough to make your stomach growl. Main Street runs north to the great North Gate, whose iron-bound doors stay shut and barred against the road beyond. South, the street descends toward the busy heart of the port. Flour dust whitens the doorstep and the gutter beside it.
rooms.12004: This small kitchen is little more than a soot-blackened roof on posts, built against the outer wall of the main warehouse to feed the porters. A brick hearth with an iron spit fills one side, and a long trestle table scarred by knives stands before it. Smoke curls out from under the eaves into the grey sky. The warehouse door lies to the north, and a path leads east to the First-Aid Station.
rooms.12011: A canvas awning stretched between two posts shelters a pair of narrow cots and a scrubbed table, and that is the whole of the first-aid station. Strips of linen hang drying on a line, and a water butt stands by one post with a dipper chained to its rim. The sharp smell of vinegar and lye cannot quite cover the older smell of blood. Porters hurt by falling cargo are carried here from the river dock to the east, and the kitchen lies a few steps west.
rooms.12025: Behind a tall fence of iron bars, cargo held for the customs house waits in sealed bales and crates, each tagged with a lead seal and a number. Caged lamps hang from the beams and throw a mesh of shadow across the swept floor. A clerk's counter closes the only gap in the bars, a heavy cashbox bolted beneath it. Passages lead north toward the busy entrance hall and west to the river dock doors.
rooms.212026: Your boat rocks on the green water of the canal, hemmed in by walls of dressed stone higher than your head. Westward the channel widens beside the warehouse dock, and the great stone bulk of the warehouse looms over it. Eastward the canal runs straight toward the sea, and already the air tastes of salt. Chaff and straw from the loading bays drift in a yellow skin along the walls.
rooms.212047: Midway along its length the canal passes beneath a low timber footbridge, and you must duck as your boat slides through its shadow. Green weed hangs from the stone walls to the waterline, and the smell of the tide grows stronger with every stroke. The water runs on east toward the ocean side docks and back west toward the warehouse. Overhead, the wheels of a cart rumble across the planks of the bridge.
rooms.212052: The canal broadens as it nears the sea, and its walls fall back to low quays of tarred timber. Your boat begins to lift and settle on the first long breaths of swell rolling in from open water. East of here the canal mouth bristles with the cranes and hoists of the unloading dock. Westward the channel narrows again between high stone walls.
rooms.12054: The canal spills out here into the harbour, and the chop slaps hard against the pilings of the unloading dock. A great wooden crane leans out over the water, its hook swinging on a chain as thick as your wrist. North of your boat a covered loading dock opens onto the quay, the shoreline runs away east, and the broad harbour of Port Halyon spreads to the south. The canal leads back west into the town.
rooms.12064: A long roof of tarred planks covers this loading dock, and the gloom beneath it smells of hemp, pitch and bilge water. Pegs along the walls hold coils of hawser, and a chalked board lists the hours of the tides. A heavy gate in the west wall opens onto the East Gate of Port Halyon. Northward the planking runs out into daylight along the Dock of Port Halyon, and to the south it ends at the lip of the canal.
rooms.12057: The dock runs out over a hump of black rock here, and tufts of sea pink and coarse grass cling in its cracks. Wind off the water snaps at your clothes and carries the cries of gulls from the rooftops. Eastward, the rock breaks into ledges above the shoreline, where small boats put out. The dock continues north toward the ocean end, and the covered loading dock lies south.
rooms.212066: Broad planks, grey and split by sun and salt, carry the dock out over the water on a forest of tarred piles. Iron bollards squat along the edge, wound with frayed rope and speckled white with droppings. Through the gaps between the boards you can see green water heaving beneath your feet. The dock runs on north to its far end and back south toward the town, and a boat can push off east into the shallows.
rooms.212067: The dock ends in a square platform of heavy beams, open on three sides to wind and spray. A tall post at its corner carries an iron lantern cage, black with soot, to guide boats home after dark. On the east side a weed-slick landing stage meets the water, where the shoreline currents tug at anything afloat. The planks lead back south toward the town.
rooms.8801: Your boat bobs in the lee of the ocean dock, where the water is dark green and laced with weed. The shore curves away south in a line of rocks and pale shingle, white with breaking foam. East of here the swell lifts and lengthens as it rolls in from the Sea of Storms. The landing stage at the end of the dock lies close by to the west.
rooms.8805: Clear of the dock, your boat meets the first real swell of the Sea of Storms, and its bow rises and slaps down in a burst of spray. Back to the west the roofs of Port Halyon huddle along the shore under a smudge of chimney smoke. The water here is grey-green and cold, streaked with foam. Open sea stretches away east and south as far as you can see.
rooms.8810: A long, slow swell rolls under the hull, lifting the boat high enough to glimpse the whole curve of the coast before dropping it into a trough of green water. Ragged clouds race low overhead, and far out a squall trails grey veils of rain across the horizon. Your boat's timbers creak with every roll. The sea runs on east and south, and the port lies back to the west.
rooms.8816: Spray whips off the wave crests here and stings your eyes with salt. A bell buoy, anchored over some hidden shoal, clangs mournfully as it heaves on the swell. The water around it is paler, almost jade, where the sand rises close beneath the surface. The open sea continues east and south, and the coast falls slowly away to the west.
rooms.8823: The coast is only a dark line behind you now, and the sea has turned the colour of slate. Whitecaps break all around, and a hard, steady wind heels the boat over. Cold water slops in over the gunwale and swills about your feet. Far out, a bank of thunderheads piles high on the horizon, lit from within by silent flickers.
rooms.8831: A broken mast juts from the sea here at a drunken angle, all that shows of some ship that foundered on a shoal. Weed streams from its crosstree, and the swell breaks white around its foot. The water is clear enough that you can make out the dark ribs of the hull beneath the surface. Open sea runs east and south, and the long way back to port lies west.
rooms.8840: Rain sweeps across the water in hissing curtains, flattening the wave tops and blurring the horizon into grey nothing. Your boat wallows in a confused sea, struck by waves from two sides at once. Water streams from your hair and runs in cold trickles inside your collar. The rain thins a little to the east, while south and west the sea vanishes into murk.
rooms.8849: Long rollers march out of the east in endless ranks, each one lifting your boat and passing on beneath it toward the distant shore. Between them the troughs are deep enough to hide the horizon, so that for a moment there is nothing but walls of moving water. A cold wind drives flecks of foam across the surface like blown snow. To the south the sea grows darker still.
rooms.8857: The wind drops almost to nothing here, and the sea heaves in a sullen, oily calm beneath a sky the colour of lead. The air smells sharply of the coming storm, and the hair on your arms prickles. Far off to the east a pale waterspout twists from the clouds and stalks across the water. The same eerie stillness lies over the sea to the south and west.
rooms.8864: Out here no land shows in any direction, and the sea is a heaving plain of dark water under a low ceiling of cloud. The wind keens over the waves and fills your ears with a ceaseless roar. Your boat climbs each swell sluggishly, heavy with bilge water. The waves roll on east and south without end, and the way back lies west.
rooms.8870: Lightning cracks across the sky close by, and the thunder that follows seems to shake the water itself. In the flash you glimpse the whole sea in white and black, every crest frozen for an instant. Rain drums on your shoulders and dances in pale spikes on the surface. Toward the east the sky shows a sickly yellow light, while south the water runs into deeper darkness.
rooms.8875: Here the swell runs into a belt of broken, churning water, as if the sea itself refused to go any further. Beyond it lies only spume and a wall of fog that nothing can pierce. Your boat yaws and twists in the turmoil, its oars biting on foam. Calmer water lies south, and the long road home runs back west.
rooms.8876: A strong current runs along the edge of the sea here, setting your boat steadily south whether you will or no. The water is a deep, clear blue and bitterly cold, and long ropes of kelp sway in its depths. A grey wall of fog hangs beyond the current, hiding whatever lies past it. Broken water churns to the north, and westward the open sea rolls on.
rooms.8877: Fog creeps out over the water here, and the world shrinks to a few boat lengths of grey sea. Sounds carry strangely, so that the slap of a wave seems to come from overhead and once you could swear you hear a bell. Mist beads on the gunwales and drips from your eyebrows. The current tugs you on south, though clearer water lies west and the way north is open.
rooms.8878: The current bends sharply here around a reef of black rock that breaks the surface in a long line of foam. Waves burst against it with a deep, hollow boom, and spray hangs over the rocks in a drifting veil. No boat could pass through those breakers. The current swings back north along the fog, and open water lies west.
rooms.8873: The boom of the reef carries from the east, and now and then a gust brings a fine salt rain of its spray. The water here is choppy and confused, its crests slapping at the hull from every side. A gnarled log, bleached silver by sun and salt, rolls lazily in the swell. Open sea stretches north, south and west.
rooms.8872: Patches of fog drift across the water from the east like slow grey sails. Between them the sea glitters under a stray shaft of sunlight, then dulls again to pewter. A raft of brown weed and cork net floats turns slowly in an eddy, rising and falling with the waves. The swell runs north and south, and open water spreads west.
rooms.8871: The sea here is a deep ink-blue, so dark that the waves look carved from stone until they break. Cold water wells up from the depths and chills the air, so that your breath smokes. Foam lies on the surface in long streaks that point the way the wind is blowing. Water stretches north, east, south and west, with no landmark to steer by.
rooms.8865: Here the wind has torn the cloud apart, and a hard blue sky shows through the gaps. Sunlight flashes off the wave tops so brightly that you must squint, and the sea turns from grey to a cold, glittering green. Spray dries to a crust of salt on your skin and clothes. The broad sea rolls on in every direction, its darker water lying south.
rooms.8866: A deep, sullen swell rolls in from the south, each wave long, smooth-backed and heavy with the weight of the open ocean. Your boat rides them easily enough, rising and falling like a slow breath. Now and then a gust lifts a fine smoke of spindrift from the crests. Open water spreads east, west and north.
rooms.8867: Dark tide rips cut across the sea here, lines of brown, frothing water where two currents grind together. Your boat lurches as it crosses one, spinning half about before you can steady it. Weed and splintered driftwood gather along the rips in long, ragged windrows. Southward, tall dark shapes rise from the water at the edge of sight.
rooms.8868: To the west the Basalt Pillars of Stethelos rise from the sea, great columns of black stone standing in a ragged rank like the ruins of some drowned hall. The swell booms hollowly among their feet and throws up fountains of spray. The water around your boat is restless, eddying back from the pillars in sudden swirls. Open sea lies north, east and south.
rooms.8874: Here the Sea of Storms gives way to the open ocean, and its short, angry chop smooths into a long and powerful swell. The water deepens to a clear, bottomless blue. Southward a current gathers strength and flows away into the ocean, while the rougher sea lies north. The basalt pillars stand dark and distant to the west.
rooms.9503: The ocean here is warmer and bluer than the storm sea, and a steady current carries your boat along. To the north the grey water of the Sea of Storms heaves under its clouds, while the sky overhead is clearing. Westward the tarred piles of a long pier stand out of the water. The current runs on south, smooth and strong.
rooms.9504: The ocean is calm and immense here, its surface creased by a long, lazy swell. Clumps of yellow weed slide past your boat, all drifting the same way. Dark clouds still hang along the horizon to the north where the storm sea lies. The current pulls you on south, toward a place where the water seems to bend.
rooms.9505: The current flowing from the north swings through a wide curve here and runs away east. You can see the bend in the water itself, a long smooth crease edged with a lace of foam. The sun lies warm on your neck, and the ocean is empty to every horizon.
rooms.9506: The current flowing in from the west turns again here and pours away south. The water heaps against itself at the turn in a ridge of short, steep waves. Your boat slews and rocks as it is caught and carried round. The ocean all around is a deep, dazzling blue beneath a clean sky.
rooms.9507: Two currents meet and wrestle here, raising a patch of choppy water that hisses and slaps against the hull. One stream comes from the north and the other pulls east, and between them your boat spins uncertainly. Foam and bubbles boil up through the surface as if the sea were simmering. Beyond the turmoil the ocean lies calm and blue.
rooms.9509: The water runs smooth and deep here, carrying your boat south in a long, easy glide. The ocean is so clear that sunlight slants into it in wavering golden shafts that never find a bottom. Back to the west the cross-currents still churn white. A warm wind blows from somewhere far off, smelling faintly of flowers and green land.
rooms.9510: The ocean opens out here, vast and deep, and three currents meet in a great slow whirl of blue water. One runs in from the north, another sets east toward the masts of an island port, and a third curls away west. Your boat turns lazily on the swirl like a leaf on a millpond. Beneath the glittering surface the water looks almost black.
rooms.9518: A small island rises from the ocean here, its harbour walls of pale stone wrapped around a huddle of red roofs and a stubby lighthouse. A heavy chain boom hangs across the harbour mouth, bearded with green weed, and there is no gap in it for a boat. Thin smoke rises from a chimney or two beyond the wall. The current runs north along the island's shore, and the deep cross-currents lie back to the west.
rooms.9519: A strong current runs north and south here, carrying your boat along the island's rocky shore. Waves break on black rocks a stone's throw away, and behind them the slopes rise green with scrub and wind-twisted pines. The air smells of resin and warm stone. The chained harbour mouth lies south, and northward the current bears you away from the island.
rooms.9520: The current flows here like a broad river through the ocean, north toward a patch of troubled water and south toward the island. Lines of drifting foam mark its edges, and beyond them the sea is almost still. Your boat runs along between those lines as if on a road. The water is a deep turquoise, warm when you trail a hand in it.
rooms.9535: Currents from three directions collide here, churning the water into a mess of peaked, slapping waves. A slow whirl of foam turns in the middle of it all. The northern stream leads toward a green island, the southern back toward a walled harbour, and an eastern branch slides off into open sea. Spray rattles against the hull like thrown gravel.
rooms.9543: The current runs swiftly north here toward a wooded island whose cliffs rise sheer from the sea. Its pull is so strong that rowing back south toward the cross-currents is hard, sweaty work. The cliffs are streaked white by generations of nesting birds. The water darkens as it runs into the island's shadow.
rooms.9544: Here the current, arriving from the south, curls along the foot of the island's cliffs and bends away west. Sea caves gape in the rock just above the waterline, too narrow for a boat, and boom like drums as the swell surges into them. The island towers over you, its crown dark with pines. Cold spray drifts from the cliff foot and beads on your skin.
rooms.9545: The current hugs the island here, sweeping your boat past a narrow strip of grey shingle hemmed in by cliffs. Each wave rattles the pebbles as it drains back, a sound like a long indrawn breath. The current is too strong to let you land, and bears you on around the shore. The island curves away north, and the sea caves lie back to the east.
rooms.9546: On this side of the island the cliffs give way to steep slopes of grass and wildflowers that tumble to the water's edge. A roofless stone hut stands on a ledge above the shore, its doorway staring out to sea. The scent of thyme drifts out over the water. The current swings east along the shore from here, and south back toward the shingle beach.
rooms.9547: The current runs fast and straight here, squeezed between the island and a line of half-sunken rocks. White water foams over the rocks with every swell, and your boat shoots along the channel like an arrow. On the island a stream falls from the hillside in a silver thread and spills into the sea. The channel runs on east and back west.
rooms.9548: The current rounds the last point of the island here and turns south toward a long wooden pier. A tall stone pillar stands on the point, carved with weathered spirals and crowned by a bronze dish gone green with age. Gentle swells lap at the foot of the pillar. The narrow channel between the rocks lies back to the west.
rooms.9549: To the west a long pier of silvered timber runs out from the island, and beyond it a road winds away between flowering trees. A tall gate of iron bars closes the landward end of the pier, so thickly grown with vines and white blossom that it cannot have opened in years. A sweet scent drifts across the water from the gardens beyond. The current runs back north around the point.
rooms.9530: The ocean here is crossed by a tangle of currents, its surface a patchwork of glassy slicks and broken water. Your boat glides across a smooth patch, then bucks as it strikes a band of chop. One stream sets north toward a sharp turn, another curves away south, and a third runs back west. Far off, the sun glints on something white at the edge of the world.
rooms.9537: The current turns hard here, almost doubling back on itself, and your boat is flung round so sharply that you must grab the gunwale. Water mounds on the outside of the bend in a smooth, glassy hump. The stream arriving from the south swings away east. A faint mist hangs over the turn, cool and salty on your face.
rooms.9538: The current bends gently here, curving from west to north in a long, lazy arc. The water is calmer than at the sharp turn, and you can rest your arms a while. Far to the north a smudge of land lies along the horizon, half lost in haze. Sunlight dapples the swell in shifting coins of gold.
rooms.9541: The current arriving from the south snaps round a sharp corner here and races off east. In that direction two long stone moles reach out into the sea, marking the entrance to a harbour. The water is quick and ruffled, and your boat skips over it like a flat stone. A smell of woodsmoke drifts out across the water.
rooms.9542: Two long moles of tumbled stone reach out into the ocean here, and between them the current flows south into a quiet harbour channel. A white lighthouse stands at the tip of one mole, its lamp burning with a pale, steady glow that never flickers. Beyond the moles the water is flat and still as glass. Back west, the current races round its sharp turn.
rooms.9540: The current runs north and south here through the channel between the two moles. The water is eerily still, and your boat slides over it without a ripple or a sound. Strangely, no weed or barnacle clings to the stones of the moles, which look as fresh as the day they were laid. South lies the harbor to Timeless Island, wrapped in a golden haze.
rooms.9539: The harbor to Timeless Island opens before you, its quays of pale gold stone glowing in a light that seems to come from nowhere. Yet however hard you row south toward them, the current curls gently round and sets you back where you began. The air is warm and utterly still, and the water holds the sky like a mirror. Only the way north, back through the channel, leads anywhere at all.
rooms.9524: The current curves here from north to east, and on the bend the water slows into a broad, quiet pool. Rafts of amber weed, studded with tiny air bladders, collect there and turn in slow circles. The sun is fierce here, and the air shimmers above the water. Your boat drifts lazily before the current picks it up again.
rooms.9529: Open ocean surrounds you here, empty and blue to the rim of the world. A light breeze ruffles the water into tiny wavelets that glitter like scattered glass. The current runs south toward a patch of troubled water and west toward a quiet, weed-strewn bend. Your boat's shadow slides along beneath you on the clear water.
rooms.9528: Here the currents collide in a broad, seething patch, and ridges of white water run across it like ploughed furrows. Your boat is tossed from one ridge to the next, its timbers groaning. Calmer streams lead away north, east and west. The noise of the churning water drowns out even the wind.
rooms.9532: Here a current running north and south crosses another that flows in from the west, and the water turns in a slow, broad eddy. At its heart a dimple of spinning water sucks in flecks of foam. Your boat circles once, then twice, before you can pull clear. The sky above is a pale, washed blue.
rooms.9533: A narrow current runs north and south here, a ribbon of darker blue laid across the paler sea. On either side the water lies still and bright, flashing back the sun. A faint smell of rain rides the breeze from the north. Your boat settles into the stream as if it knows the way.
rooms.9534: The ocean here turns in a lazy circle, and rowing west only brings you round to the same patch of water. A small squall passes overhead, pattering on the sea and freshening the air. Rainwater gathers in the bottom of your boat. Only the current running south seems to lead anywhere.
rooms.9531: The current flows north and south here, strong and smooth, between two long ridges of standing waves. Your boat runs along the channel between them like a cartwheel in a rut. Beyond the ridges the sea is broken and wild, while inside them the water is almost glassy. Spray from the standing waves drifts over you in a fine, cool mist.
rooms.9536: The current sweeps from north to west here in a wide, curving bend. On the outside of the curve the water runs fast and ruffled, while on the inside it lies smooth and dark. Far off, a bank of grey cloud sits low upon the sea. A cool wind blows across the bend and raises gooseflesh on your arms.
rooms.9526: Currents from the north, east and south crash together here, heaping the water into steep, pointed waves that collapse as fast as they rise. The water has a strange chill to it, and the light has turned flat and grey. Somewhere beyond the haze a deep, slow tolling rolls across the water. Your boat pitches wildly, shipping spray at every plunge.
rooms.9527: Grey haze lies over the ocean here, softening the horizon and muffling every sound. The swell is long and low, and the water has a cold, leaden look. One current slides away south toward churning water, and another runs west. Drops of mist gather on your sleeves and run together.
rooms.9522: The currents that meet here are cold ones, and the air above their clash is thick with drifting mist. Waves come at your boat from every quarter, slapping and sucking at the hull. Through gaps in the mist you glimpse the dark shape of an island, far off and low. Streams of moving water lead away north, east and south.
rooms.9523: The current whips round a sharp corner here, turning between south and east so suddenly that the water stands in a short, steep wall. Your boat heels over and spins half round before it rights itself. Weed and foam are flung out of the turn into the calmer sea beyond. Overhead the clouds are thickening.
rooms.9521: A cold current runs north and south here, dark as slate and moving fast. The haze has thickened into a low fog that drifts over the water in rags. On the cold air comes a faint smell of wet earth and rot. The water hisses along the hull as the current hurries you on, and your breath clouds before your face.
rooms.9516: Currents tangle here in a broad stretch of uneasy water, and the fog thins enough to show a low grey island off in the murk. A strong stream sets away west, fast and dark, while gentler currents lead north and east. The water slaps irritably at the boat, never settling into a rhythm. Cold drops fall from the fog like slow rain.
rooms.9525: Here a current from the north runs into another bending west, and the water between them heaves and knots. Tall, smooth-backed swells pass beneath you without breaking. The clouds hang so low that they seem to brush the wave tops. Your boat climbs and drops with a slow, queasy rhythm.
rooms.9515: A strong current races from west to east here, hurrying your boat along. Close by to the north rises a low grey island, its shore lined with dead trees and leaning stones. Its one landing is shut off by a row of sharpened stakes driven into the shallows and bound with rusted chain, and no boat can pass them. The wind off the island smells of cold ash.
rooms.9514: A powerful current gathers itself here and begins its long run east, tugging hard at your boat. The water to the north lies calmer, sheltered by an island whose pier reaches out into the sea. Long streamers of weed point along the flow like pennants in a wind. It would take strong arms to row against this stream.
rooms.9513: To the east a rickety pier runs toward an island beach heaped with wreckage, broken barrels and bleached spars. Its outer end is blocked by a barricade of lashed timbers, and the planks behind it have rotted through in a dozen places. Everything on the island seems oddly still, as though it were waiting for something. Currents lead away south and west.
rooms.9512: The current turns sharply here, swinging between north and east around a hidden ledge of rock that shows as a pale shadow beneath the surface. Water boils over the ledge in a hump of foam, and your boat scrapes past it with a shudder. East of the turn a rickety pier juts from an island. The wind here blows steady and cool.
rooms.9511: The current kinks sharply here, bending between east and south around a broad patch of pale, shallow water. A sandbar glimmers gold through the clear sea, so near the surface that your oars brush against it. Eastward the deep ocean turns in its slow great whirl. The sun is hot here, and the glare off the water makes your eyes ache.
rooms.9502: The Ocean Pier stands on tall piles to the south, its timbers green with weed below the tide line. A landing stage at its end lets boats come alongside out of the swell. The water is calm in the pier's lee, clear enough to see the sandy bottom ribbed by the tide. Open ocean stretches away north and east.
rooms.9501: The ocean meets a long reef here, marked by a line of breakers that no boat could hope to cross. Over the reef's edge the water turns a vivid, milky green. The roar of the surf is constant, and a fine haze of spray hangs in the air. The only open water lies back south toward the Ocean Pier.
rooms.9500: The Ocean Pier runs a long way out over the water on tarred piles, its planks bleached grey and warped by the sun. Iron cleats along its edges are worn bright by mooring ropes, and the boards smell of tar, salt and fish. North, the pier ends at a landing stage above the open ocean. South, it meets the shore at Port Harem, where painted lanterns hang from the eaves.
rooms.12101: Port Harem is little more than a scatter of gaudy houses along a sandy shore, their shutters painted crimson and gold and peeling in the salt air. Coloured lanterns sway on poles along the sand, and the breeze carries a cloying smell of perfume and spilled wine. Behind the houses the dunes are tufted with spiky sea holly. The Ocean Pier stretches out over the water to the north, and a path follows the beach east toward a grander house on a rise.
rooms.12102: A grand old house sits on a sandy rise above the beach, its walls washed pink and its windows screened with carved lattices. Broad steps lead down through its garden to a lower door, from which drift soft music and the scent of incense. Wind-bent palms rattle their fronds overhead. Port Harem lies west along the shore, and Beach Road leads away east.
rooms.12103: Beach Road is a track of packed sand and crushed shells running along the top of the shore. On one side the surf rolls in long and lazy over a pale beach, and on the other dunes crowned with marram grass hide the land beyond. Shells crunch under every step. The road runs east toward a dark hill and west to the pink house on its rise.
rooms.12105: The road turns its back on the sea here and heads east toward the dark bulk of Vice Hill. Sand gives way to hard earth, and the grass along the verges is brown and trampled. A weathered post leans beside the road, its sign long since torn away. Behind you to the west the sound of the surf fades.
rooms.12139: Vice Hill rises steep and stony here, its slopes choked with thorny scrub and stunted, leaning trees. One path scrambles up toward the summit, and another drops down the hillside into a fold of shadow. Creepy Road runs off east between dead hedges, while Beach Road leads back west toward the sea. A crooked signpost stands at the crossing, its arms pointing every which way.
rooms.12106: Creepy Road earns its name quickly, for the hedges on either side are dead and grey and their bare twigs knot together overhead like clutching fingers. The sky shows through them only in dull scraps. No bird sings, and your footsteps sound too loud on the hard earth. The road runs on east and back west to Vice Hill.
rooms.12107: Here the dead hedges give way to a sagging iron fence, its spikes capped with the bleached skulls of small animals. Beyond it a field of grey weeds stretches toward a tall, dark building with a single tower. A cold wind moans through the railings. The road continues east toward the building and west between the hedges.
rooms.12108: Creepy Road ends here before the Building of Fear, a tall house of black-stained timber that leans over the road as though listening. Its windows are dark, and its crooked tower leans the other way. Two carved posts flank the path, each topped with a grinning wooden face. The door stands open a crack to the east, and the road leads back west.
rooms.12145: The front hall of the Building of Fear is tall and narrow, panelled in dark wood that has warped and split with damp. A single lamp burns with a sickly green flame above the door, making the shadows twitch and jump. A threadbare red runner leads east into a room hung with tapestries, and the door behind you opens west onto Creepy Road. Somewhere deep in the house a floorboard creaks.
rooms.12146: Huge tapestries cover every wall of this long room, faded to the colours of dried blood and old bruises. They show scenes of terror: a ship dragged under by a vast serpent, a city in flames, and a crowd fleeing from something the weaver never finished. The eyes of the woven figures seem to follow you as you cross the floor. Doorways lead east to a room of trophies and west to the entrance hall.
rooms.12148: Mounted heads glare from every wall of this room, boar and bear and stag, and at the end of the row a few that look unpleasantly human. Glass cases along the walls hold rusted blades and yellowed bones, each with a neat brass label. Dust lies thick on the glass, though the heads themselves are oddly clean. A heavy door to the north bears a snarling stone face, a passage leads east toward a tower, and doorways open south and west.
rooms.12147: Stone gargoyles crouch on pedestals all around this round, windowless room, wings half spread and mouths gaping in silent howls. Their eyes are chips of red glass that catch the light of a lamp hanging from the ceiling. The air is cold, and each time you look away you could swear one of them has shifted. The only door leads back south to the trophy room.
rooms.12150: This is the foot of a tall, hollow tower, and the wind that creeps in through its cracks sets up a thin, endless wailing that rises and falls like a voice. A spiral stair of rusted iron climbs up into the darkness overhead. The stone walls are damp and streaked with orange stains. A passage leads back west to the trophy room.
rooms.12151: The iron staircase spirals up through the hollow tower, its steps narrow and slick with damp. Each step rings faintly underfoot, and the wailing of the wind is louder here, coming from everywhere at once. A rail of twisted iron is all that keeps you from the drop. Above you the stair ends at an oddly angled doorway, and below it winds down to the tower's foot.
rooms.12153: Nothing in this hallway is quite square, for the walls lean inward, the floor tilts, and the ceiling sags so low at one end that you must stoop. Doors are set at odd angles to the north, east and south, and no two of them are the same size. A narrow stair climbs up to the floor above, and the iron staircase leads down into the tower. Looking along the hallway for long makes your head swim.
rooms.12154: A great open hearth fills one wall of this room, wide enough to roast an ox whole, its stones blackened by years of fires. Embers still glow among the ashes, and their heat is welcome after the chill of the halls, though the smoke smells oddly sweet. Iron hooks and chains hang in the mouth of the chimney. The only door leads back south.
rooms.12155: Shelves climb every wall of this cramped storeroom, crowded with jars, sacks and stoppered bottles. Some of the jars hold pale shapes floating in cloudy liquid, and you decide not to look too closely. Hooks on the beams hold coils of rope, bundles of black candles and lengths of chain. A smell of tallow and vinegar hangs in the air, and the door leads back west.
rooms.12152: This tiny cell has no window, only a barred slot in the door to the north that lets in a little grey light. Mouldy straw is heaped in one corner beneath an iron ring set into the wall, from which hangs a short chain. The plaster is covered in scratches, hundreds of them, as though someone had tried to dig out with bare fingernails. The air smells of damp and old fear.
rooms.12157: This hallway crosses the upper floor of the house, its walls papered in a pattern of dark vines that seem to writhe at the edge of your sight. A carved door to the east bears a brass plate engraved with the words High Priest of Fear, and a plainer door opens to the south. Candles gutter in sconces along the walls, though no draught can be felt. The hall runs on north and west, and a narrow stair leads down to the crooked hallway below.
rooms.12159: The hallway ends here at a narrow black door set into the north wall. Portraits in heavy frames line the walls, and though the faces differ, every one has the same pale, staring eyes. The paint has darkened and cracked everywhere but on those eyes, which look wet and freshly done. The hallway leads back south.
rooms.12160: This closet is barely large enough to turn around in, and it reeks of camphor with something sourer underneath. Moth-eaten robes of black and crimson hang from a rail, rustling faintly though the air is still. Long scratches score the inside of the door, at about the height of a child. The door opens south onto the hallway.
rooms.12158: The High Priest of Fear keeps a richly furnished office, with a great desk of black wood, shelves of leather-bound books and a rug the colour of old wine. A silver mask twisted into a scream hangs on the wall behind the desk, catching the lamplight. Heavy incense smoulders in a bronze bowl, and its sweet, choking smoke clings to everything. The only way out is the door to the west.
rooms.12156: A four-poster bed stands in the middle of this room, its curtains torn and its covers flung back as if someone fled in the night. Dust lies thick over everything, and the mirror of the dressing table has been smashed into a web of cracks. In one corner a wooden rocking horse creaks gently to and fro, though nothing has touched it. The door leads back north.
rooms.12161: The hallway turns a corner here, and the floor seems to slope away from you whichever way you face. A tall case clock stands against the wall, ticking loudly, though its hands never move from a quarter to midnight. The wallpaper here has been torn away in long strips, baring grey plaster beneath. The hall runs north and east.
rooms.12162: The hallway narrows here between walls draped in black crepe, and the ceiling is so low that cobwebs brush your hair. Somewhere inside the walls a faint knocking starts, stops, and starts again. The loose floorboards groan under your weight. Each candle sconce along the wall holds only a stub of melted black wax. The hall runs on north and back south.
rooms.12163: A pair of tall glass doors at this end of the hallway open west onto a balcony, and a breath of fresh air drifts in through them. After the stale gloom of the house it smells wonderfully of salt and rain. Damp has blistered the wallpaper around the doors, and a dark stain spreads over the floorboards. The hall leads back south into the house.
rooms.12164: This narrow balcony juts from the wall of the Building of Fear high above the ground, its iron railing rusted and loose. From here you can see the whole of Vice Hill, the dead hedges of Creepy Road, and beyond them the grey glitter of the sea. The wind tugs at your clothes, and rain clouds scud low across the sky. Glass doors lead back east into the house.
rooms.12149: Rails of costumes crowd this room, black robes and ragged shrouds and masks of grinning skulls and weeping saints. A long mirror ringed with dim lamps covers one wall, and the table beneath it is crusted with white greasepaint and smears of false blood. It seems that some of the terrors of this house are made by hand. The only door leads north to the trophy room.
rooms.12123: Near the top of Vice Hill the scrub thins to bare rock and black, tar-smeared earth. Tunnel mouths gape in the hillside to the east and the west, their rims caulked with pitch like the seams of a ship. A rutted track heads north as Tarry Road, a path climbs up into a dark stand of trees, and the way down leads back to the crossroads. The whole hilltop smells of hot tar.
rooms.12124: Tarry Road is a rutted track of black earth, so soaked with spilled pitch that it clings to your boots. Rusted barrel hoops and charred staves are half buried in the verges, and the grass between them is dead. A bitter smoke hangs low over the ground. The road runs north between low hummocks and south to the crown of Vice Hill.
rooms.12125: The road passes a pit of bubbling black tar here, fenced off by a few crooked stakes. Bubbles swell and burst on its surface with lazy pops, each one releasing a puff of stinking smoke. Near the edge, the bleached ribs of some large beast poke out of the tar. The track runs on north and back south.
rooms.12126: Tarry Road ends at a long, low building of tarred black planks, half sunk into the hillside. Its door hangs open to the east, and beyond it a bare corridor runs away into the dark. Thistles grow tall around the walls, but nothing at all grows on the road. The track leads back south toward Vice Hill.
rooms.12180: This bare corridor is lined with tarred planks that sweat sticky beads of pitch. Dust and dead leaves have blown in through the doorway to the west, where grey daylight shows. Another doorway to the east opens onto blackness so thick it seems solid, and the corridor runs on north. Your footsteps echo as if the place were empty for miles.
rooms.12181: Here the corridor is crossed by a wider passage, and the tarred planks give way to rough stone. To the west a tall archway leads toward the Hall of Hopelessness, and to the east another doorway opens into darkness. An iron bracket on the wall holds the charred stump of a torch that burned out long ago. The corridor runs on north and south.
rooms.12182: The corridor comes to an end against a blank stone wall, and a broad opening to the west leads into a great square chamber. Rows of old notices are nailed beside the opening, their ink faded beyond reading. Grit crunches underfoot, and the air is stale and dry. The corridor runs back south.
rooms.12178: This great square chamber lies beneath a vaulted stone roof, so large that the light of its few lamps never reaches the corners. A dry fountain stands at its heart, the basin heaped with grey ash. Wooden stairs climb up to a gallery, a stone stair leads down into the depths, and doorways open north, east and south. Every sound you make comes back to you a moment late.
rooms.12167: Long tables run the length of this narrow room, each place on them marked with a painted number. The tables are bare now, but pale outlines in the dust show where boots, belts and purses were once laid out for counting. A clerk's high desk stands by the door to the north, and the great square lies back south. A chill hangs in the air, as if the room remembers every one of them.
rooms.12166: An iron lattice divides this bare room in two, so that those on one side can be looked over from the other like beasts at a fair. A bench bolted to the floor has been worn smooth by many nervous hands. Behind a heavy, iron-banded door to the north lies a room that smells of hot metal and old blood. The outlay lies back south.
rooms.12179: A tall arch of black stone marks the entrance to the Hall of Hopelessness, and words are carved deep into its keystone. Beneath the arch a tunnel sealed with tar runs away south into darkness, breathing out a cold draught that smells of pitch and damp. The great square lies north, and a deserted corridor leads east. The flagstones beneath the arch are worn into hollows by dragging feet.
rooms.12121: Thick black tar seals the stone blocks of this tunnel, oozing from the joints and hanging in sticky drips from the roof. The air is close and warm, and the reek of pitch catches in your throat. A faint glow from the archway to the north gives the only light, while southward the tunnel runs on into blackness. Your boots stick and unstick from the floor with every step.
rooms.12119: The tunnel runs straight and utterly dark here, the tarred walls swallowing what little light you carry. Handprints are pressed into the soft tar at shoulder height, as though others felt their way along here blind. Some of the prints are very small. The tunnel runs on north and south.
rooms.12117: Water drips from the roof here, beading on the tar and creeping along the walls in slow black rivulets. A shallow gutter cut in the floor carries it away, and its gurgle echoes through the dark. The air is cooler here and smells of wet stone as well as pitch. North and south, the passage fades into darkness.
rooms.12115: A rusted iron grate is set into the tunnel wall here, covering a vent no wider than your fist. Through it drifts a faint, far-off sound like many voices chanting together. Tar has oozed over the grate and set into black icicles along its lower bars. The passage leads on to the north and back to the south.
rooms.12113: The tunnel bends a little here, and a niche in the wall holds a crude clay figure of a hooded man, its face smeared black with tar. Old candle wax has dribbled over its feet in pale, lumpy layers. The darkness seems to press in from both ends of the passage. Past the niche the tunnel goes on north and south.
rooms.12111: The tunnel opens east onto the slopes of Vice Hill, and a grey wash of daylight seeps in to show walls black and glistening with tar. Just inside the mouth the floor is scored with long gouges, as if something heavy had been dragged through. Northward the passage runs straight into blackness. The smell of pitch is strong enough to make your eyes water.
rooms.12173: This low room has the look of a storeroom put to darker uses. Pegs along the walls hold leg irons and lengths of chain, each with a number chalked above it. A long table in the middle is stained with spilled ink and darker blotches. The only way on is a doorway to the north.
rooms.12172: Hard wooden benches line the walls of this cheerless room, and the floor before them is worn into grooves by restless feet. Names, dates and short prayers are scratched into every inch of the wood. A lamp on a chain gives a weak yellow light that makes the wait feel longer. The way out leads west, toward muffled sounds you would rather not name.
rooms.12170: A heavy chair with leather straps on its arms and legs is bolted to the floor here, facing a plain wooden desk. A shuttered lantern on the desk is angled to shine full in the face of whoever sits in the chair. The walls are padded with stained canvas to deaden every sound. Doorways lead east to another waiting room and south into darkness.
rooms.12169: This waiting room is smaller and colder than it needs to be, its whitewashed walls bare of any comfort. A row of iron rings runs along one wall at waist height, a few still trailing short chains. A stone trough of stale water stands in the corner, skinned with dust. The interrogation room lies west, and a narrow doorway leads north.
rooms.12168: Bins of rough planks line the walls of this cramped room, each one marked with a letter and empty now save for a few rags. A brass scale for weighing coin stands on a shelf, its pans green with verdigris. Someone has chalked long columns of figures on the wall, adding up to a total that has been angrily scrubbed out. The only way out is back south.

5251.description: The basin is cut from a single block of red stone, its rim worn smooth by the hands of those who warmed themselves here long ago. The flame rises from a crack in its floor and never wavers, not even when a draught stirs the sand.

12033.description: The milestone bears the name of Garathorm cut in tall, old-fashioned letters, with a number of leagues beneath it. Weather and the hands of travellers have worn the figures so smooth that the distance could be almost anything.

212067.description: The iron cage at the top of the post is big enough to hold a fire basket, and its bars are crusted with soot and salt. Notches cut into the post mark the heights of great tides, the highest of them level with your chin.

8816.description: The buoy is a squat iron barrel scabbed with barnacles, with a cracked bronze bell hung in a cage on top. Every heave of the sea swings the clapper, so that it is never quite silent.

8831.description: The mast is as thick as a man's waist and still wears a few turns of rotten rigging. A board is nailed to it just above the waterline, but whatever was painted there has long since been scoured away.

8868.description: Each pillar is six-sided, as neat as if a mason had cut it, and the tallest stand higher than a ship's mast. Sailors say they are the gateposts of a city the sea swallowed long ago, and that in a dead calm its bells can still be heard.

9518.description: The boom is a chain of iron links each as long as your forearm, slung between two squat towers and held up with tarred barrels. From the weed and rust on it, it has not been lowered in years.

9548.description: The spirals wind inward to a single carved eye at the heart of the stone. The bronze dish on top is blackened inside, as though fires were once lit there to guide boats around the point.

9549.description: The bars of the gate are wrought into leaves and hanging fruit, and a heavy lock rusted solid holds it shut. Through the vines you glimpse a road of pale stone climbing into a green and sunlit country.

9539.description: Beyond the quays rise white towers and terraces, and on the tallest stands a great clock whose hands do not move. The longer you look at it, the less sure you are of how long you have been looking.

9515.description: The stakes are black with age and as thick as a man's leg, their points turned out toward the sea. Whoever drove them in meant to keep something from landing, or something from leaving.

12139.description: The signpost's arms have been turned and nailed back so many times that none of them can be trusted. Someone has carved a grinning face into the post, and someone else has tried to hack it out again.

12108.description: The faces on the posts are carved with wide, staring eyes and far too many teeth. Rain has run black streaks from their eyes, so that they seem to weep as they grin.

12146.description: The largest tapestry shows a tall figure in a pale mask standing over a kneeling crowd. Its face has been picked away thread by thread, as if someone could not bear to look at it.

12158.description: The silver is beaten thin and polished to a mirror, so that your own face stares back at you through the screaming mouth. Small hooks along its edge show that it was made to be worn.

12125.description: The pit is perhaps ten paces across, and there is no telling how deep it goes. A stake driven in at its edge has sunk until only its tip shows, as though the pit were slowly swallowing it.

12179.description: The carved words read: Leave Hope With Those Who Wait For You. Beneath them someone has scratched a row of tally marks that stops in the middle of a group.

creatures.long_desc: A grey harbour gull struts along the planks, eyeing you for scraps.
creatures.description: A big, heavy-bodied gull with a yellow bill hooked at the tip and a spot of red near its end. Its pale eyes are cold and calculating, and its feathers smell of fish and tar. It shows no fear of you at all.

creatures.long_desc: A green shore crab scuttles sideways over the sand, claws raised.
creatures.description: A broad-backed crab the size of a dinner plate, its shell mottled green and brown like weedy rock. It holds its claws up and open, ready to pinch anything that comes too close, and its stalked eyes swivel to follow you.

creatures.long_desc: A banded sea snake ripples through the water, its flat tail sculling.
creatures.description: A slender snake ringed in black and pale blue, with a tail flattened like an oar blade. It swims with lazy grace, but its small head is quick, and its bite carries a numbing venom.
rooms: On The Canal By The Ocean Side Unloading Dock
In the ocean by the Ocean Pier

creatures.long_desc: A blue shark circles just below the surface, its fin slicing the swell.
creatures.description: A long, slender shark with a deep blue back and a white belly, its snout pointed and its eyes flat and black. It moves without seeming effort, and the teeth in its half-open jaws are serrated like saws.

creatures.long_desc: A great hammerhead shark sweeps past, swinging its broad head from side to side.
creatures.description: Its head is drawn out into a flat bar with an eye at either end, and it swings it to and fro as it hunts. It is longer than a rowing boat, grey-brown above and pale beneath, and its flanks are scored with old scars.
rooms: At a sharp turn in the current
At a bend in the current

creatures.long_desc: A great sea serpent rears from the waves, water streaming from its scaly coils.
creatures.description: Coil after coil of green-black scales rolls through the sea, each loop as thick as a barrel, while a long head crested with ragged fins sways high above the water. Its eyes are the yellow of old lamplight, and its breath stinks of the deep.
rooms: At cross-currents in the deep, wide ocean

creatures.long_desc: A veiled desert raider watches you with narrowed eyes, a curved blade in his fist.
creatures.description: He is wrapped from head to foot in sand-coloured cloth, with only a slit for his dark, narrowed eyes. A curved blade hangs at his hip, and stolen rings and amulets clink on a cord at his belt. The hidden chambers under the sand are his band's bolt-hole.

creatures.long_desc: A tar-stained smuggler lurks in the shadows, a knife held low and ready.
creatures.description: His hands and forearms are black with pitch to the elbow, and his clothes are stiff with it. He has a sailor's rolling gait and a sailor's squint, and he watches you the way a man watches a fat purse.

creatures.long_desc: A hooded cultist of terror glides through the gloom, murmuring a litany of dread.
creatures.description: Beneath the black hood is a face painted chalk-white, with dark smudges around the eyes to make them seem hollow. The robe is stitched with screaming mouths in red thread, and a long knife hangs from a cord at the waist.

creatures.long_desc: A wax effigy stands stiffly among the shadows, its glass eyes catching the light.
creatures.description: From a few paces away it could pass for a living man, but up close the skin is waxen and faintly shiny, and the painted lips never move. Here and there the wax has sagged and run, and something dark and hollow shows beneath it.

creatures.long_desc: A hollow-eyed shade drifts here, its mouth shaping words that never come.
creatures.description: It is the grey, wavering outline of a man in rags, with shackles on its wrists that make no sound. Its eyes are empty pits, and when it turns them on you a terrible weariness drags at your limbs. One fist stays clenched around something it will not let go, as if it has been waiting a very long time to pay its way out.
rooms: Entrance To The Hall Of Hopelessness

items.room_desc: A sailor's rigging knife lies here, its grip bound in tarred twine.
items.description: A short knife with a narrow, wickedly pointed blade, made for working rope and splicing lines but just as handy in a brawl. Its wooden grip is bound in tarred twine that will not slip in a wet hand.

items.room_desc: A pair of grey sharkskin boots stands here, stiff with salt.
items.description: These boots are cut from rough grey sharkskin that rasps like a file against your palm. They are stitched with gut and sealed at the seams with pitch, and they keep out the wet better than any leather.

items.room_desc: A white mask frozen in a scream lies here, staring at nothing.
items.description: A mask of stiffened white leather shaped into a face caught in mid-scream, its eyeholes ringed with black paint. Behind it you feel the faint, cold thrill of being the thing that others fear.

items.room_desc: A tarnished coin of strange design glints dully here.
items.description: A heavy coin of dark, unfamiliar metal, struck with a crowned figure whose face has worn away and with letters no living scholar can read. Such coins are said to come from drowned Carcosa, and the dead were once laid to rest with one to pay their passage. It stays cold no matter how long you hold it.

items.room_desc: A goatskin water flask stitched with blue thread lies here.
items.description: A flask of goatskin sealed with resin and stitched with blue desert patterns, slung from a plaited cord. The water inside stays cool long after the sun should have warmed it, and a long swallow puts the strength back into tired limbs.
